Project evidence: https://github.com/aaryanadiger/VajraSetu. README.md, docs/ARCHITECTURE.md, docs/SCANNER_AND_CALIBRATION.md and docs/OPERATIONS_AND_SAFETY.md, inspected 26 October 2026. Expo SDK 57 documentation read at https://docs.expo.dev/versions/v57.0.0/. Current scanner uses deterministic known-layout sampling, RGB/Lab/CIEDE2000 and provisional thresholds. The original deck's calibrated ML estimator and perspective correction are future design objectives, not implemented or validated capabilities. FeSO4 expiry and quantitative exposure estimates remain provisional. No claim of clinical, field, or regulatory validation is made.
Original approach retained: OpenCV preprocessing, region detection, reference normalisation, lighting compensation, RGB/CIELAB/DeltaE colour features, quantitative calibration and a local worker record. Spatial colour features, robust perspective correction and calibrated ML are planned original-design goals, not current validated capabilities. Current processing uses bounded central-card extraction, reference white balance, CIEDE2000 and three-frame consistency checks. Scan quality is an imaging metric, not chemical confidence.
The complete supplied 30 ppm test series: 0,5,10,15,30 minutes; calculated cumulative doses 0,2.5,5,7.5,15 ppm*h. Dose = concentration * duration. This chart is arithmetic, not an accuracy curve. Calibration v2 includes a pooled intermediate response because the supplied 5/15 minute colours overlap. Saturated dose is a lower bound. Fixed eight-hour TWA = cumulative dose / 8 hours, not actual recorded shift duration. The record schema includes worker/band metadata, dates, fixed reference shift, validity and provisional estimates.
Disclosures requested by KHOJ p11: app uses React Native/Expo, native OpenCV and Expo SQLite; bundled local language copy with optional Sarvam translation/cache for non-core strings in supported languages. There is no trained image ML model or cloud image upload in the current scan path. Code and detailed architecture: https://github.com/aaryanadiger/VajraSetu. [1] is background on interpreting direct instrument exposure records, not validation of a passive band.

text: Original deck cost targets, not vendor quotes. Confirm through procurement, calibration and field trials. Assumes 26 shifts/month.

Original source: https://www.canva.com/design/DAHVkQadZBA/8sKx2MfSjISZCmg6W30OqA/edit, slide 4, Working cost model. Every original allocation retained: Starter band INR20 = body/fastener8 + reference/expiry4 + assembly3 + packaging/QC3 + distribution2. Shift strip INR1.00 = Tyvek substrate0.25 + CuSO4 chemistry0.25 + reference/print0.15 + cutting/QC0.35. 100 workers: INR2000 initial setup plus INR2600/month. Monthly arithmetic is 100 workers * 26 shifts/month * INR1 per replacement strip; 26 is the assumption implicit in the original total. These are design allocation targets, not verified quotations, sales prices, margins or a complete operating budget. Phones, validation, training, taxes and support are not included in the original model.
The original separately proposes a disposable INR1/band variant, while the detailed INR1 allocation is for the replacement shift strip. The slide preserves that distinction rather than claiming the whole disposable product has a validated bill of materials. Original band-format intent: reusable for demanding conditions and sustainability, disposable for cost-sensitive routine shifts. Local manufacturing and commercially available components are opportunities subject to supplier confirmation.
Original positioning retained: electronic detector = live ppm/alarms, battery/calibration; passive badge/tube = cumulative visual/manual record; VajraSetu = colour-to-phone record and low-cost target. The passive band cannot replace certified gas detection.

text: Impact is proposed, not measured. Pilot gates: calibration and stability, held-out devices/batches, language review and EHS approval.

Original source: https://www.canva.com/design/DAHVkQadZBA/8sKx2MfSjISZCmg6W30OqA/edit, slides 4 and 5. All original impact themes retained: worker safety/awareness, industrial usability, digital safety records and Make in India. The goal is to support interpretation of a cumulative passive signal alongside direct instruments, not to claim reduced illness, validated personal dosimetry or emergency protection. Proposed pilot beneficiaries include industrial workers and supervisors; healthcare relevance is prevention-oriented occupational health and traceable workplace review.
All original challenge/response rows retained. Privacy response (on-device encryption and role-based access) and standard template exports are design goals, not implemented security or integration claims. Offline SQLite logging and bundled language copy exist. Reusable/disposable band alternatives address durability and cost. The implementation has one local worker profile, not multi-role remote access.
Original rollout stages retained: prototype, controlled field validation, phased deployment. Before a field trial, calibrate the final formulation and exact batch, test stability/aged expiry controls and interference, hold out devices/operators/batches, measure false-valid/category/retry rates, validate native language wording, complete EHS review and agree pilot success criteria.
